Query OpenSearch as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__opensearch.R
oauth_db_opensearch_api.Rd

Search OpenSearch documents and calculate summaries using each visitor's permissions. An index holds the documents you query. The client supports JSON searches and the SQL plugin, returning results as R lists.

Usage

oauth_db_opensearch_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS OpenSearch cluster base URL, including a proxy path if needed.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one HTTP operation, including a read retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with these methods:

  • $search(index = NULL, body = list(), query = list(), raw = FALSE) searches an index using an OpenSearch JSON query. The index can be a name, pattern or character vector; NULL searches across the cluster.

  • $sql(sql, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) runs a query through the SQL plugin and returns its native JSON result.

  • $request(path, method = "GET", query = list(), body = NULL, raw = FALSE) calls a JSON API. Supply relative path segments, such as c("orders", "_doc", "42").

Details

Configure OpenSearch's Security plugin to accept your provider's tokens and map the user and role claims to OpenSearch permissions. The endpoint must accept bearer tokens; AWS SigV4 needs a different client.

Create the client inside server() and call its methods from render or reactive expressions. Each operation uses a current token and discards results after sign-out or account changes. GET and HEAD can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401; POST searches, SQL and writes don't retry.

Search results keep hits, aggregations and totals as R lists. SQL results keep their schema and datarows. Large integers stay as strings. Use raw = TRUE for an httr2 response. Searches reporting a timeout or failed shards raise an error unless you request the raw response.

SQL parameters and pagination

SQL requires the server's SQL plugin. Use ? placeholders with an unnamed list of typed values, such as list(list(type = "integer", value = 30)) in parameters.

Fetch search pages explicitly with from/size or search_after. Use $request() for SQL cursors and other JSON APIs; consume or close cursors before changing accounts.

See also

vignette("opensearch", package = "shinyOAuthDB"). oauth_db_demo() runs a local OpenSearch and Keycloak example.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
search <- oauth_db_opensearch_api(auth$connection,
  url = "https://search.example.org")
output$results <- shiny::renderPrint({
  search$search("orders", body = list(
    size = 20L, query = list(term = list(country = "NL"))
  ))$hits
})
} # }
